description: Admin dashboard with statistics and data management: modern dashboard UI with 4 stat cards, line chart, status breakdown, recent submissions table, employee import from Excel/CSV with pandas validation and per-row commit (FINDING #7), user management with user-to-employee linking, TAS records export with date filter fix (FINDING #10) and empty results handling (FINDING #8), manager_id null parsing (FINDING #9)
steps: In app/routes/admin.py, create admin_bp blueprint

Implement GET /admin/dashboard with @admin_required: query total TAS count, pending count, approved this month count (submitted_at >= first day of current month using datetime.now().replace(day=1, hour=0, minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0)), rejected count and rejection rate %; query TAS submissions by date for last 7 days (func.count, cast(submitted_at, Date), group by date, order by date); query status breakdown counts (Pending/Approved/Rejected); query 10 most recent TAS with employee join ordered by submitted_at desc; render admin/dashboard.html with all data

Create app/templates/admin/dashboard.html extending base.html: 4 stat cards in responsive grid (TOTAL TAS purple bg var(--card-purple), PENDING APPROVALS green var(--card-green), APPROVED blue var(--card-blue), REJECTED orange var(--card-peach) with rejection rate); charts section 2-column layout (left 8/12 width line chart 'TAS Submissions Over Time' div id='tasChart' with Chart.js, right 4/12 status breakdown with colored progress bars); recent submissions table (10 rows, columns: TAS Number, Employee Name, Destination, Travel Date, Status, each row links to /admin/tas/<tas_id>) with id='dashboard-recent-table'; 'View All TAS Records' link button to /admin/tas_list

In app/static/js/main.js, add Chart.js initialization: read chart data from template via JSON in script tag, create line chart on canvas id='tasChart' with labels from dates array and data from counts array, primary blue color var(--primary-blue), responsive; add DataTables initialization for #dashboard-recent-table with paging: false, searching: false, info: false, order: [[0, 'desc']]
In app/forms.py, create ImportEmployeeForm with file field (FileRequired, FileAllowed(['xlsx', 'csv'])), submit button
Implement GET /admin/import_employees with @admin_required: render admin/import_employees.html with form

Implement POST /admin/import_employees: validate file presence and extension (.xlsx/.csv only), save to UPLOAD_FOLDER with secure_filename(), read with pandas (pd.read_excel for xlsx, pd.read_csv for csv); validate required columns ['emp_id', 'name', 'email'] present else flash error with missing columns; validate row count <= 1000 else flash 'File contains more than 1000 rows. Please split the file.'; validate no duplicate emp_id within file using emp_ids_in_file.duplicated() else flash duplicate emp_ids; validate no duplicate email within file else flash duplicate emails

Continue POST /admin/import_employees: iterate df.iterrows() with per-row validation and commit (partial success by design per FINDING #7): validate emp_id non-empty and <= 20 chars, name non-empty and <= 255 chars, email regex match and <= 255 chars; parse manager_id with pd.isna(manager_id_raw) check for NaN then str().strip() then check if manager_id.lower() in ['', 'none', 'null', 'n/a', 'na'] set to None (FINDING #9); validate manager_id != emp_id; detect simple two-way circular reference (if manager_id in file, check manager's manager_id != emp_id); create or update Employee record with all fields; per-row try/except around db.session.commit() collecting success_count and error_rows with row number and error message; flash success_count and up to 10 errors; cleanup temp file in finally block with try/except on os.remove()

Create app/templates/admin/import_employees.html extending base.html: form with file input accept='.xlsx,.csv', validation info box (required columns: emp_id, name, email; optional: department, designation, manager_id; row limit: 1000; formats: .xlsx or .csv; duplicate handling: updates existing emp_id), submit button, CSRF token via {{ form.hidden_tag() }}

Create sample_employees.csv in project root with columns: emp_id,name,email,department,designation,manager_id; include 5 sample rows (e.g., 1987,John Doe,john@example.com,IT,Manager,; 1988,Jane Smith,jane@example.com,IT,Developer,1987; 1989,Bob Johnson,bob@example.com,HR,Manager,; 1990,Alice Williams,alice@example.com,Finance,Analyst,; 1991,Charlie Brown,charlie@example.com,IT,Developer,1987)

In app/forms.py, create CreateUserForm with username (DataRequired, Length(3,50), Regexp(r'^[a-zA-Z0-9_]+$' message='Username must contain only letters, numbers, and underscores')), password PasswordField (DataRequired, Length(min=8)), role SelectField choices=[('admin','Admin'),('employee','Employee')] (DataRequired), emp_id SelectField (Optional, coerce=lambda x: x or None), is_active BooleanField default=True, submit; add validate_emp_id method: if self.role.data == 'employee' and not field.data raise ValidationError('Employee ID is required for employee role')
Implement GET /admin/user_management with @admin_required: query all users with LEFT JOIN employee (User.query.outerjoin(Employee).all()), render admin/user_management.html with users list

Create app/templates/admin/user_management.html extending base.html: table with columns (Username, Role, Linked Employee showing name and emp_id, Status showing is_active, Actions with edit/deactivate buttons if needed); 'Create New User' button links to /admin/create_user

Implement GET /admin/create_user with @admin_required: populate emp_id choices with employees not linked to any user (db.session.query(Employee).outerjoin(User).filter(User.user_id == None).all()), add ('', 'None (for admin users)') option first; render admin/create_user.html with form

Implement POST /admin/create_user: validate form, additional check: if role=='employee' and not emp_id flash error 'Employee ID is required for employee role'; check emp_id not already linked (User.query.filter_by(emp_id=emp_id).first() returns None); create User with username, role, emp_id or None, is_active; call user.set_password(password) in try/except ValueError catching password < 8 chars validation; db.session.add and commit in try/except (ValueError for password, IntegrityError for duplicate username or emp_id, general Exception for other errors) with rollback and flash error; on success flash 'User {username} created successfully' and redirect to user_management

Create app/templates/admin/create_user.html extending base.html: form with fields (username text input, password password input, role dropdown with admin/employee options, emp_id dropdown populated from backend with employees not linked, is_active checkbox default checked), validation errors display with Bootstrap alert-danger, submit button, CSRF token via {{ form.hidden_tag() }}

Implement GET /admin/export_tas with @admin_required: parse query params (format default 'xlsx', status default 'All', date_from optional, date_to optional, department optional); validate dates with try/except ValueError, if date_from > date_to return 400 error JSON {'error': 'date_from must be before date_to'}; build query: TASRecord join Employee, select tas_number, emp_id, employee.name, email, department, designation, travel_from, travel_to, travel_date_start, travel_date_end, purpose, estimated_cost, status, submitted_at, reviewed_at; apply filters: if status != 'All' filter by status, if date_from filter submitted_at >= datetime.fromisoformat(date_from), if date_to filter submitted_at < datetime.fromisoformat(date_to) + timedelta(days=1) to include full day (FINDING #10), if department filter by department; execute query.all()

Continue GET /admin/export_tas: handle empty results (FINDING #8): if not results create df = pd.DataFrame(columns=['TAS Number', 'Employee ID', 'Employee Name', 'Email', 'Department', 'Designation', 'From', 'To', 'Start Date', 'End Date', 'Purpose', 'Estimated Cost', 'Status', 'Submitted At', 'Reviewed At']) else df = pd.DataFrame(results, columns=[...]); generate timestamp filename tas_records_{timestamp}.{format}; save to UPLOAD_FOLDER with df.to_csv or df.to_excel (engine='openpyxl'); define cleanup_file function that tries os.remove with except logging warning; return send_file with as_attachment, download_name, mimetype (text/csv or application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet); call response.call_on_close(cleanup_file)

In app/utils.py, add cleanup_old_exports(hours=24) function: iterate os.listdir(UPLOAD_FOLDER) for filenames starting with 'tas_records_', check os.path.getmtime < datetime.now() - timedelta(hours=hours), try os.remove with except logging error; log info on successful cleanup

Update README.md to add section 'Scheduled Cleanup': 'Run cleanup_old_exports() daily via cron (Linux/Mac) or Task Scheduler (Windows) to remove export files older than 24 hours. Example cron: 0 2 * * * /path/to/venv/bin/python -c "from app.utils import cleanup_old_exports; from app import create_app; app = create_app(); with app.app_context(): cleanup_old_exports()"'
Register admin_bp blueprint in app/__init__.py create_app function with app.register_blueprint(admin_bp, url_prefix='/admin')

In app/static/css/style.css, add styles for stat cards: .stat-card with border-radius, box-shadow var(--shadow), padding, responsive grid (.stats-grid with display: grid, grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(250px, 1fr)), gap: 1.5rem); card backgrounds using CSS variables; progress bars for status breakdown with colored backgrounds
acceptance_criteria: Admin dashboard accessible at /admin/dashboard with @admin_required protection
Dashboard displays 4 stat cards with correct counts from database (purple, green, blue, orange backgrounds)
Dashboard line chart renders with Chart.js showing TAS submissions by date (empty if no data)
Dashboard status breakdown shows Pending/Approved/Rejected counts with progress bars
Dashboard recent submissions table shows 10 most recent TAS with DataTables (no pagination/search)
Import employees page accessible at /admin/import_employees
Import validates file format (.xlsx/.csv), required columns, row limit (1000), duplicate emp_id, duplicate email
Import parses manager_id handling pandas NaN and common null representations (none, null, n/a)
Import commits per-row with partial success (if row 50 fails, rows 1-49 already saved)
Import displays success count and up to 10 error messages
sample_employees.csv created with 5 test employees
User management page lists all users with linked employee info
Create user form validates username (alphanumeric+underscore, 3-50 chars), password (min 8), role, emp_id (required for employee role)
Create user prevents linking emp_id already linked to another user
Export TAS page accessible at /admin/export_tas with query param filters
Export handles empty results by creating DataFrame with explicit columns (headers only)
Export date_to filter includes full day using +1 day and < operator
Export generates .xlsx or .csv file with timestamp in filename
Export file auto-cleanup via response.call_on_close()
cleanup_old_exports() function removes export files older than 24 hours
README.md includes scheduled cleanup instructions
verification: Login as admin, navigate to /admin/dashboard - page renders with 4 stat cards (all zeros initially), empty chart, empty recent table
Navigate to /admin/import_employees, upload sample_employees.csv - flash shows 'Successfully imported 5 employees'
Check database: 'mysql -u root -p tas_erp -e "SELECT emp_id, name, email FROM employees;"' - shows 5 employees
Re-upload same sample_employees.csv - flash shows '5 employees' and database has 5 rows (updates, not duplicates)
Upload file with missing 'email' column - flash shows 'Missing required columns: email'
Upload file > 10MB - flash shows 'File too large. Maximum size is 10 MB.'
Upload CSV with duplicate emp_id within file - flash shows 'Duplicate emp_id found in file: {id}'
Upload CSV with invalid email format - flash shows error for that row, other valid rows imported (partial success)
Navigate to /admin/user_management - shows admin user in table
Click 'Create New User', create employee user: username=john_doe, password=password123, role=employee, emp_id=1987 (John Doe), is_active=checked - flash shows 'User john_doe created successfully'
Check database: 'mysql -u root -p tas_erp -e "SELECT username, role, emp_id FROM users;"' - shows admin and john_doe
Attempt to create user with same username - flash shows 'Username already exists' or similar IntegrityError message
Attempt to create employee user without emp_id - flash shows 'Employee ID is required for employee role'
Attempt to create user linking emp_id 1987 again - flash shows 'This employee already has a user account'
Create admin user without emp_id - succeeds with emp_id=NULL
Navigate to /admin/export_tas (no TAS records yet) - file downloads with headers only, open in Excel and verify columns present
Create a test TAS record manually in database or via employee portal (requires FEAT-003), then test export with format=xlsx - downloads .xlsx file with data
Test export with status=Pending - only Pending TAS in file
Test export with date_from=2024-01-01&date_to=2024-01-31 - only TAS submitted in January in file
Test export CSV format - downloads .csv file
Check UPLOAD_FOLDER after export download - file should be cleaned up (may remain briefly due to response streaming)

Manually create old file in UPLOAD_FOLDER named tas_records_20240101_120000.xlsx with mtime > 24 hours ago (touch command or manual), run cleanup_old_exports() via Python shell - file deleted and logged
Navigate to /admin/dashboard after importing employees - stat cards still show zeros (no TAS records yet, expected)
findings: Admin data management complete. Design review findings #7 (import partial success), #8 (export empty results), #9 (manager_id null parsing), #10 (date_to full day) resolved in this feature. Dashboard UI ready. Employee import tested with sample data. User management allows linking users to employees.
